headline: Robotaxi companies keep cameras inside their cars, and privacy experts say few clear US rules limit how the footage can be used.
score_reason: Lowered from 5: WIRED’s headline says riders are being spied on, but the article shows broad privacy policies and company claims of limited viewing, not proven misuse.
importance_line: Anyone who rides in one of these robotaxis can be filmed inside the car and few clear rules limit how the footage is used, which matters first to riders; the article shows broad company policies rather than proven misuse of rider footage.
summary: WIRED reports that Waymo, Zoox and Tesla robotaxis carry cameras inside the cabin, which the companies say help keep riders safe and enforce rules, with staff viewing them only when needed. Their privacy policies also allow footage to be used to improve products or services, and experts quoted by WIRED say few clear US rules govern this kind of surveillance.
notes: Full article read. Feature piece, no single dated event. Score lowered by 1 because the headline overstates what the article shows.
